newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Rupiah jumps after Indonesia's surprise move.
newsitem.headline: Rupiah jumps after Indonesia's surprise move.

text.p: The rupiah rose sharply against the dollar on Wednesday after Indonesia's central bank suprised the market and widened its intervention band for the second time this year.
The widening effectively gives the market more flexibility to set its own rate, a move which met with approval as the rupiah soared against the dollar immediately after the announcement.
Spot rupiah soared to a high of 2,326.0 against the dollar by midday, compared with an opening of 2,348.50/49.50. At 0919 GMT, it was quoted at 2,329.00/31.00
The rupiah was fixed by the central bank at 2,309/2,501 rupiah against the dollar on Wednesday against 2,344.0/2,462.0 on Tuesday, or a spread of eight percent against five percent.

The central bank said in a statement obtained by Reuters that the move was in line with policies to contain a overheating economy, to reduce speculative trading, to strengthen the ability of the bank to control currency fluctuations and to give more solid ground for monetary control.
The band, fixed daily by the central bank, sets the limits outside of which the central bank will intervene in the foreign exchange market.
"The timing caught the market by surprise," Edwin Png, country treasurer of Bank of America, told Reuters.
"It shows that the central bank has the determination to let the market decide what is the right level of the currency."

He added that that the central bank was quite encouraged by the last move since the market had been trading within the band. Bank Indonesia last widened its intervention band in June this year to five percent from three percent after the rupiah came under persistent upward pressure.
"I think the market is mature enough to accept this. The market is pretty professional in that there was not much panic after the announcement," Png said.

Currency dealers said Wednesday's rise was in line with gains after previous widenings of the intervention band. They said prevailing market sentiment that the rupiah was a high-yielding currency also helped the gains.
Png said the rupiah was likely to remain strong until the end of the year because of its attractive yield compared with Thailand's baht or other regional currencies.
The central bank also announced that that banks' minimum reserve requirement ratio would be increased to five percent from three percent, effective April 16, 1997.
The reserve requirement is the amount of deposits banks must place with the central bank. Bank Indonesia last raised its reserve requirement to three percent from two percent in February.
The central bank said all other existing reserve requirements would remain unchanged, including calculations and reporting methods.

It said the increase in the reserve ratio and the widening of the intervention band would enable the government to contain loan growth and overall liquidity in the market as well as increase the effectiveness of monetary management.
